In these models, taxonomic resolution is a major concern.
That is, we need to consider whether a model that groups many different species together into one functional unit can decribe the aggregate population dynamics accurately enough to have useful predictive power.
In the case of the croaker,

's detailed statistical analysis led them to conclude that even one functional category for this species alone is insufficient.
That was because the life history parameters – survival, mortality and fecundity – differ so dramatically between year classes, and between larval and juvenile stages within the first year class, that it was not possible to understand the impacts of natural and human factors in population declines without accounting for these categories separately.
